title: Iterators
learningGoals: walk a container with begin and end

youtube.title: C++ Iterators: begin, end and More | C++ Programming EP 76
youtube.description: In this episode you will walk a container with begin and end, use reverse iterators and avoid skipping items when you erase, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Iterators · 0:55 Walk with an iterator · 1:35 Begin and end · 2:05 Second program · 3:05 Recap · 3:35 Bug of the Day · 4:23 Challenge · 4:43 Next episode

scenes.narration: Today we learn the idea behind every loop in the library. An iterator is like a pointer for a container.

scenes.onScreen: "Iterators": numbered lines (1. An iterator points at one item; 2. Star reads the item, plus plus moves on; 3. End is one past the last item) and an analogy card: a finger on a train timetable: it points to one line, and moves to the next
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: An iterator points at one item in a container. Star reads the item. Plus plus moves to the next one. Begin points at the first item. End points one past the last item. You stop when you reach end. The same code works for vector, list, set and map. Think of a finger on a train timetable. It points at one line, and moves to the next.

scenes.onScreen: iter.cpp: a for loop with begin and end
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 7] The iterator starts at the first item. [HL 7] The loop stops when it reaches end. [HL 7] Plus plus moves to the next item. [HL 8] Star reads the item. [HL 11] Rbegin starts at the last item. [HL 11] Rend marks the position before the first. Plus plus moves backwards. The output is thirty, twenty, ten.

scenes.onScreen: a table: positions of begin and end
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: Begin points at ten. Begin plus one points at twenty. Begin plus two points at thirty. End points one past the last item. You never read from end. You only compare against it.

diagram.caption: a table: positions of begin and end

scenes.onScreen: advance.cpp: next and distance help with iterators
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 7] A list is not an array. You cannot write begin plus two. [HL 8] Next moves an iterator forward by a number of steps. It works for every container. [HL 9] The item is fifteen. [HL 10] Distance counts the steps between two iterators. The answer is two.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as advance dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints fifteen, and then two.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. An iterator points at one item. Two. Star reads, and plus plus moves on. Three. End is one past the last item. Four. The same loop works for every container. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: Erasing and skipping
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program runs and the wrong output appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We erase all even numbers, but four stays in the vector. Erase already returns the next item. Then the loop moves on again, and skips it. Move the iterator only when you did not erase.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the iterator never get lost? It always knew where end was.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why did the iterator never get lost? It always knew where end was.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: remove all negative numbers
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write a loop with iterators that removes all negative numbers from a vector. Do not skip any item. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.onScreen: Next: EP 77 · Algorithms from the library
scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: We end module eight here. Next time: the algorithm library, and sorting with one line. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Program output (it runs, but the answer is wrong):

4 7
bug.why: Erase returns the iterator of the next item. The loop then moves on again, and skips that item. Move on only in the else branch.

pun: "Why did the iterator never get lost? It always knew where end was."
challenge: Write a loop with iterators that removes all negative numbers from a vector. Do not skip any item.
challengeAnswer: Use a for loop with no step. If the item is negative, set it to the result of erase. Otherwise, move it on.
